text:
Noah Warren is getting a real look in his first NHL season, and the Ducks are still deciding how much to lean on him. The 22-year-old from Montreal, a 6-foot-5, 233-pound right shot taken 42nd overall in 2022, has played every one of Anaheim's last ten games, but his minutes have swung from 10.9 to 21.6 depending on the night. He plays a heavy game, 41 hits and 28 blocked shots in 20 games, and Stefen Rosner of NHL.com noted him tripping Brayden Schenn for an Islanders power play on Saturday.

The six assists are a nice start (defensemen drafted around his slot scored a median 0.21 points a game in their first full season; he is at 0.30), but 20 games is a small sample and the underlying picture is rougher. Anaheim takes about half the shot attempts with him on the ice at five on five, yet only 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), almost eight points worse than without him. Opponents get the better looks when he is out there. That gap, more than the points, is what decides whether his ice time settles at the high end of that range.
headline: Noah Warren's rookie minutes are still being sorted out
